doc.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Replacing Beverly Peer in Bobby Short's band; Short's background
summary: Tate joined Bobby Short in December 1996, and describes Short's career and home.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: I see you’ve worked with some great singers too.

Bobby, a singer to end all singers. Oh I’ve been with him full time for four and a half years. I replaced a guy named Beverly Peer, a man that had been with the Chick Webb band. He was 84 when he resigned, in the middle of a night. He couldn’t get through the second set. He was very ill and Bobby called me up and Bobby said, “What are you doing?” I had rehearsed with him that day and the day before. Rehearsed the show. Because that Beverly was on the brink. And Bobby called me at nine o’clock and says, “What are you doing?” I said, “I’m in my pajamas watching T.V.” And Bobby said, “Well you’d better get your ass into your tuxedo and get in here because it’s starting, the second show, and it’s going to be televised for Brazilian television.” And I had music spread — Bobby didn’t like music on the stand, and of course I memorized it all as quickly as I could and got rid of it. And these like Opus, these like medleys, and pages flopping around and everything. But I got through it and Beverly died within five or six weeks. He died mid-January, and I came in back around the fifth or sixth of December of ’96. And Beverly didn’t stay around very long. But he worked right up until the end. He was with Bobby for 38 years and I told Bobby, that night I came on I said, “Hey I want 38 years.” And I did the math and realized it would make me 91. And he said, “Well what do you think that’s going to make me?” So I said, “Okay well let’s try for ten.” And he said okay. So I’m not quite half way through the ten year plan and then I’m going to re-negotiate with him again. And he’s doing fine.
Does he go from coast — or from Europe?

He lives in, he has a place in the South of France, I believe it’s called Mouzon. My French is kind of not real strong, but he has, it’s referred to as a villa. And I’ve seen pictures of it and it is, and he’s got orchards, and he’s got 3-1/2 acres and a pool and a nice apartment in New York. He’s had a heck of a career. Started very early. He had some lean times but he went out to L.A. when he was eighteen and he just sort of went out there and placed himself on the A list where he’s been ever since. He worked for the right people, played the right music, was very smart, spoke French when he was in high school. He went on the road when he was eleven with a tutor. He said, “I had to become a man when I was eleven and then when I was fourteen,” he said. “I went back to Danville, Illinois I had to start being a boy again.” Because somebody would say something about somebody and Bobby’d say, “Oh I know him.” And they’d say, “Oh you’re such a big

shot.” And then Bobby said I had to forget about all of that and go back to school and be a high school boy again. And then he went out to California and bought himself a big black Cadillac convertible, riding around Hollywood when he was eighteen or nineteen, maybe twenty, in a convertible. He’s extremely interesting and talent like from day one. Tremendous ears. Hears everything. Totally self taught and he’s a joy to work for.
